title: Context Engineering & Repository Instructions
description: Give agents the right persistent and task-specific context while avoiding noisy, stale, or unsafe instructions.

lessons.title: Context is a scarce resource
lessons.principle: More context is not automatically better; irrelevant material can distract the model.
lessons.practice: Supply the smallest set of authoritative files and facts needed for the decision.

lessons.title: Prefer source-of-truth files
lessons.principle: Summaries can drift from implementation.
lessons.practice: Point agents to current schemas, tests, interfaces, and configuration before secondary documentation.

lessons.title: Use repository instructions
lessons.principle: Persistent instructions make recurring conventions discoverable to coding agents.
lessons.practice: Store build commands, architecture rules, test expectations, and review standards in supported repository instruction files.

lessons.title: Keep instructions actionable
lessons.principle: Long philosophy documents are easy to ignore or misapply.
lessons.practice: Write short rules that tell the agent what to inspect, preserve, run, or avoid.

lessons.title: Scope instructions by path
lessons.principle: Different directories can have different frameworks and constraints.
lessons.practice: Use path-specific guidance where supported instead of one overloaded global instruction file.

lessons.title: Document validation commands
lessons.principle: Agents need reliable feedback loops.
lessons.practice: List fast focused checks and the full pre-merge validation command.

lessons.title: Document architecture boundaries
lessons.principle: Unclear ownership encourages cross-layer coupling.
lessons.practice: State which modules own data access, domain rules, UI state, external integration, and shared utilities.

lessons.title: Document generated-code boundaries
lessons.principle: Generated files should not be hand-edited accidentally.
lessons.practice: Mark generated artifacts and identify the source command or schema that owns them.

lessons.title: Document secret boundaries
lessons.principle: Agents must know which values are sensitive and where they belong.
lessons.practice: State that secrets never enter source, prompts, logs, fixtures, or client bundles.

lessons.title: Document migration rules
lessons.principle: Schema changes can be irreversible.
lessons.practice: Describe migration naming, backward compatibility, rollout order, and rollback expectations.

lessons.title: Document testing conventions
lessons.principle: Agents otherwise invent new test styles.
lessons.practice: Point to representative tests and define where unit, integration, and end-to-end tests live.

lessons.title: Document UI conventions
lessons.principle: Visual consistency depends on reusable patterns.
lessons.practice: Identify design tokens, component libraries, accessibility rules, and responsive breakpoints.

lessons.title: Use task-local context
lessons.principle: Persistent instructions should not carry every temporary fact.
lessons.practice: Put issue-specific reproduction steps, constraints, and decisions in the task prompt or issue.

lessons.title: Refresh stale context
lessons.principle: Old architecture notes can be worse than missing documentation.
lessons.practice: Update instructions when commands, dependencies, directory structure, or team policy changes.

lessons.title: Resolve instruction conflicts
lessons.principle: Multiple instruction layers can disagree.
lessons.practice: Define precedence and keep overlapping rules consistent.

lessons.title: Avoid exposing unnecessary private data
lessons.principle: Context sent to models should be minimized to what the task needs.
lessons.practice: Exclude credentials, user data, unrelated proprietary documents, and sensitive logs.

lessons.title: Teach the agent where to look
lessons.principle: Navigation guidance reduces random code search.
lessons.practice: Name entry points, key directories, test locations, and common debugging paths.

lessons.title: Encode invariants, not trivia
lessons.principle: Persistent context should focus on rules unlikely to change every day.
lessons.practice: Document durable constraints and let the agent inspect volatile implementation details.

lessons.title: Test repository instructions
lessons.principle: Instructions are only useful if agents can follow them in real tasks.
lessons.practice: Periodically run representative tasks and refine ambiguous or ineffective guidance.

lessons.title: Treat context as infrastructure
lessons.principle: Good context engineering compounds across every AI-assisted change.
lessons.practice: Version, review, and maintain repository instructions with the same care as other development tooling.

codeExamples.snippet:
# AGENTS.md
- Run `npm test` after behavior changes.
- Keep database access in `src/data/`.
- Never commit secrets.
- Prefer existing UI primitives.

.github/instructions/ui.instructions.md
Scope: src/ui/**
- Preserve semantic HTML.
- Verify keyboard navigation.
- Use design tokens; no ad hoc colors.
